title: Day 36 · Week 5, Day 1 — Brain: three bubbles in a low-oxygen room — the first draft of the brain, the window that opens this week, and the four things that can reach it
summary: The second Brain episode, and now there is a tube. Your baby is 2–3.5 mm at Carnegie stage 10, the neural folds fusing and the heart tube forming; by the end of the week the NHS calls it a 6 mm pea. Müller & O'Rahilly's 1983 reconstructions show the forebrain, midbrain and hindbrain already visible in the open neural groove at stage 9 — the map is drawn before the tube closes — and this week the three vesicles form, the optic primordia meet at the chiasma, the hindbrain segments into rhombomeres, the otic pit sinks in and the neural crest migrates out to build the face, the ears and the heart's outflow. The neurons come later: predecessor cells walking into the forebrain before the tube is closed (Bystron 2006), cortical neuron production from about embryonic day 42 (Day 56; Stiles & Jernigan 2010), and a sequence that runs through adolescence (Rice & Barone 2000). The organogenesis window, Day 29 to about Day 70, with the neural tube's peak this week and next. Then the room the embryo is in: no maternal arterial flow into the placenta before 8 weeks, placental oxygen under 20 mmHg at 8 weeks rising to over 50 at 12, uterine-gland (histiotrophic) nutrition until week 10, and a sac built to keep oxygen out (Burton 1999, Jauniaux 2000, Rodesch 1992, Burton 2002, Jauniaux 2003) — so what reaches the brain is what is dissolved in her blood and small enough to diffuse, plus heat. Four things with numbers: heat (NTD OR 1.92 across 15 studies; hot tubs RR 2.8 in 23,491 women; fever 1.5–3× in meta-analyses, attenuated by folic acid and by treating it, and absent in 77,344 Danish pregnancies), with acetaminophen cleared by the 2.48-million-child sibling study; valproate (10.3% major malformations vs 2.9% lamotrigine in EURAP; IQ 97 vs 108 at age 6 in NEAD); isotretinoin (RR 25.6, a neural crest pattern, Lammer 1985); and alcohol and nicotine (Days 34 and 31). And the long list of things that don't reach it.
action: Two checks tonight. One: a working thermometer in the house and acetaminophen in the cabinet — buy both tomorrow if not — and agree the rule out loud: over 38 °C (100.4 °F) means acetaminophen at the box dose, fluids and a call to the practice in the morning; over 39 °C or lasting more than a day is a same-day call. Two: hot tub and sauna off the list until the tube is closed (~Day 42); revisited with numbers on Day 48. If she takes any prescription medication regularly, she calls the prescriber this week, says she's pregnant, and asks one question: is this one of the ones that matters in the first eight weeks? Not stop. Call.
